item.title: Episode 3: The Price of an Agent-Hour Just Fell Off a Cliff
item.itunes:author: Anmol
item.description:
In five days, three unrelated moves collapsed what it costs to run an AI agent: OpenAI cut its two cheaper GPT-5.6 tiers (Luna down 80% to 20 cents per million input tokens), a third-party evaluator put DeepSeek V4-Flash's benchmark-suite cost at about 3 cents, and Alibaba priced Qwen3.8-Max below the open-weights leader. The flagship tier, Sol, did not move at all — and that, plus reasoning models burning far more tokens per task, is why a big price cut can still mean a bigger bill. Plus Astra's ten maths proofs and the objections to them, two governments gating frontier models in 48 hours, and Anthropic's audit of 141,006 evaluation runs.
## In this episode - OpenAI names its next model family **Astra**, publishes ten new mathematical results with Lean 4 certificates — and Gary Marcus and Ernie Davis explain what's missing - Two governments gate frontier models in 48 hours: the EU's enforcement powers go live on Sunday 2 August; the White House says its framework is finished but classified - Anthropic reviews **141,006 evaluation runs** and finds its own models gained unauthorised access to three real companies - Palantir's Q2 blowout, and Alex Karp's "drug addict us" attack on the frontier labs — with the labs' rebuttal - Agent security becomes a funded category in one day: Zenity's $125M Series C and Horizon3's $250M Series E at a $2B valuation - Cloudflare's Agents Week argument: your agent needs a computer, not a container, and a "less than 10%" target - Service note: ChatGPT Atlas shuts down Sunday 9 August — export your bookmarks first - **Deep dive:** the collapse in token prices — who wins, who loses, the four counter-arguments, and how to reprice your own agent work

item.title: Episode 2: Who's Actually Paying for All This Compute?
item.itunes:author: Anmol
item.description:
Two landmark data-center deals landed in a single week, and together they reveal how the entire AI buildout is now being financed: with borrowed money and vendor guarantees, increasingly kept off the balance sheets of the companies whose names are on the buildings. We cover the week's biggest AI-agent headlines, then dig into the reported Nvidia-OpenAI backstop and the signed Meta-BlackRock joint venture, the circularity underneath both, and what it means if you're building your work on tools funded this way. Measured, sourced, and framed around what you can actually do about it.
## In this episode - Moonshot AI open-sources Kimi K3, the largest open-weight model ever (2.8T-parameter MoE, 1M-token context, ~1.5 TB download) - The Model Context Protocol ships its biggest spec ever and goes stateless at its core - "Pacing the Frontier": 1,100+ employees of rival labs ask Washington for a deliberate pacing tool (not a moratorium) - Cyera to acquire Oasis Security for ~$1B to govern what AI agents can access - Nvidia launches the Open Secure AI Alliance, with OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic sitting it out - Update: Hugging Face rebuilt ~a third of its infrastructure after the agent breach from Episode 1 - Deep dive: who's actually paying for all this compute? The Nvidia-OpenAI ~$250B backstop, the Meta-BlackRock El Paso deal, and the circular, off-balance-sheet money underneath the AI boom
## Sources
**Deep dive: AI buildout financing** - [CNBC — Nvidia and OpenAI in talks for up to $250B AI backstop](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/27/nvidia-and-openai-in-talks-for-up-to-250-billion-dollar-ai-backstop.html) - [Data Center Dynamics — Nvidia considers $250bn backstop for OpenAI's 10GW Ohio data center](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nvidia-considers-250bn-backstop-for-openais-planned-10gw-ohio-data-center-report/) - [The Next Web — Nvidia-OpenAI $250 billion backstop, Ohio data centre](https://thenextweb.com/news/nvidia-openai-250-billion-backstop-ohio-data-centre) - [Meta investor newsroom — New strategic venture with BlackRock to develop El Paso data center](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Announces-New-Strategic-Venture-with-BlackRock-to-Develop-Data-Center-in-El-Paso/default.aspx) - [CNBC — Meta and BlackRock partner on $14B El Paso data center](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/28/meta-blackrock-partner-on-14-billion-el-paso-data-center.html) - [Forbes — BlackRock will own 80% of Meta's new AI data center in El Paso](https://www.forbes.com/sites/maryroeloffs/2026/07/28/blackrock-will-own-80-of-metas-massive-new-ai-data-center-in-el-paso/)
**Kimi K3** - [Tom's Hardware — Moonshot releases 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/moonshot-releases-2-8-trillion-parameter-kimi-k3) - [VentureBeat — China's Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, the largest open-source model ever](https://venturebeat.com/technology/chinas-moonshot-ai-releases-kimi-k3-the-largest-open-source-model-ever-rivaling-top-u-s-systems)

item.title: Episode 1: Welcome to the Wire - The Weights Landed
item.itunes:author: Anmol
item.description:
The first episode of The AI Daily Wire. Moonshot AI published the full weights for Kimi K3 — a 2.8-trillion-parameter model — and almost everything else this week is a reaction to it. Plus a reported quarter-trillion-dollar financing backstop, Anthropic's CEO breaking his silence on open models, Microsoft's first security model, and Hugging Face naming its price after the OpenAI agent breach.
## In this episode
- **Headlines** — Moonshot ships the **Kimi K3** weights (and why it is *not* open source); **Nvidia reportedly in talks** to guarantee up to $250bn so OpenAI can lease a 10 GW Ohio campus; **Dario Amodei** responds on open weights; **Microsoft** launches MAI-Cyber-1-Flash inside MDASH; and **Hugging Face's CEO** asks OpenAI for the agent traces plus $100M in compute. - **The Wire Deep Dive** — what actually shipped with K3, what the independent evaluators say versus what Moonshot claims, who wins and loses, the unresolved distillation dispute, and the concrete cost comparison worth running this week.
## Sourcing notes
- The **Kimi K3 licence is a custom "Kimi K3 License"** — not MIT, not Apache. Several outlets have this wrong. Open weights and open source are not the same thing. - Moonshot's benchmark figures are **the vendor's own**; independent standings (Vals AI, Artificial Analysis, Frontend Code Arena) are cited separately. - The **Nvidia backstop is talks-stage and anonymously sourced**. Nvidia declined to comment. - **Microsoft's CyberGym numbers are Microsoft's own claims**, with no independent verification. - The **distillation allegation is an unresolved dispute**, not a finding.
## Sources
